zones.label: Column 1 running header
zones.note: Lexical coverage was cross-checked against the supplied Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, version 202510 (CC BY 4.0). This is a lexical aid, not a substitute transcription; the supplied BnF scan remains the authority. Source: https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html ; license: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ .

runs.text: ciar, & grangear as couſas da caſa.

lines.note: Continues the preceding page's Portuguese definition: managing or procuring the affairs of the household. The initial ciar is a word-ending, not an independent entry.
Itonami, itonamu, itonǒda gives the verb for conducting affairs or making preparations. The printed final principal part is retained, rather than modernizing the historical inflection.
Relhar completes aparelhar. Iyeuo itonamu illustrates constructing or establishing a house; the Portuguese alternative beginning Fazer continues below.

Completes the house-building example, then introduces Butçuji, with Butji explicitly preferred by Meliùs. Both Japanese forms concern Buddhist observances rather than a second house-building expression.
Uo itonamu completes the Buddhist-rites example. The translation explains arranging or preparing the ceremony; pe- continues as pera on the following row.

runs.text: ra exequias, ou commendação dalgum defunto,

lines.note: Completes pera and specifies funeral rites or a commemoration of a deceased person. The scan supports the continuous word defunto, not the OCR's de funto.

runs.text: como conuite pera os Bonzos, que lem o Foque

lines.note: An invitation or feast for the Buddhist clerics is given as an example of such preparations. Foque starts the Japanese sutra title within the Portuguese explanation and continues on the next row without a visible hyphen.

runs.text: quiǒ, & fazem outras ceremonias, &c. ou ne-

lines.note: Quiǒ completes Foquequiǒ, the sutra being read; it belongs to the embedded title despite the physical break. Other ceremonies follow, and ne- begins negociar. The title's continuation is set with the surrounding italic text.

runs.text: gociar, & aparelhar as couſas pera este officio,

lines.note: Gociar completes negociar from the preceding row. The explanation returns to arranging the things needed for this funeral office; the final conjunction continues below.
The abbreviated cõmendação completes the funeral-commemoration gloss. Its tilde is retained rather than expanding the omitted nasal letters.

runs.text: Pequenino, ou de pouca idade, co-

lines.note: Itoqenai describes someone very young or little. The Portuguese comparison begins co- and continues with children on the next row.
Mo completes como, and mininos supplies the comparison with young children. The historical vowel in mininos is preserved.
Itoqenaſa is the corresponding noun of quality, youthfulness or childishness. It is a separately indented derivative without a repeated Portuguese definition.
Itoqenǒ is the adverbial form associated with itokenai. The visible caron belongs to the printed ending and is not a nasal abbreviation.
Itori, itoru means killing by shooting. The gloss specifies an arrow or a bullet; the scan gives initial capital I and pilouro, not OCR itori and oilouro.

Itotaqe is explained by Xichicu and quanguen, string-and-wind music. Crauo starts the Portuguese comparison with a keyboard instrument, followed by a flute below; the Japanese synonyms remain ordinary roman text.

runs.text: frauta. Aliquando, Muſica deſtes dous instru-

lines.note: Frauta completes the instrument pair; Aliquando introduces the broader meaning, music from these two instruments. The final instru- has a visible division mark.
Mentos completes instrumentos. This short row closes the music gloss and does not belong to the next shooting verb.
Itouoxi, itouoſu, itouoita denotes shooting through something. The historical -oita principal part is preserved; the line ends at pi without supplying a hyphen for the continuation pilouro.
Louro completes pilouro, and de parte a parte specifies complete penetration from one side to the other. This distinguishes the verb from merely killing with a projectile above.

runs.text: Couſa de que ſe tem piedade, ou compai

lines.note: Itoxij describes an object of pity or compassionate affection. The first letter is capital I; compai continues as compaixão without a printed terminal hyphen.
Xão completes compaixão. The second construction, ter compaixão, & amor, explains the feeling of pity and love rather than supplying another headword.
Itôxiſa is the noun of the preceding compassionate quality. The scan prints a circumflex over o here although the main adjective above is unmarked; that variation is retained.
Itôxǔ is the related adverbial form. Its circumflex on o and caron on u remain distinct, without regularizing either to match the unaccented headword.

runs.text: Hũs ſinais como fios que estão no

lines.note: Itoyaqiba names thread-like marks at the blade edge. The visible word is fios, threads, which repairs OCR fos and explains the ito element of the Japanese compound.

runs.text: gume da Catana conforme à tempera do aço.

lines.note: The marks occur at the edge of the Catana according to the tempering of its steel. Catana is a Japanese-derived term embedded in the Portuguese explanation; the gloss is not a separate Japanese example.
Itoyoridai is identified only as a fish of that name. Aßi is supported by the printed final i, not OCR aßo; no modern species determination is added.
Ittai funjin describes a single substance manifesting in divided forms. The source's sustancia spelling is kept without inserting a modernizing b, and the infinitive continues below.

runs.text: ſe, ou porſe noutro lugar com diuerſo nome co

lines.note: The reflexive ſe completes diuidir; the alternative is appearing elsewhere under another name. The final co continues as como, without an inferred hyphen.
Mo completes como. The authors attribute this account of multiple manifestations to the gentios; that is the dictionary's confessional characterization, not an independent factual endorsement.

runs.text: Hum tamanino, ou breue eſpaço. Vt,

lines.note: Ittan denotes a very short interval. The diminutive-looking tamanino is retained as printed; the example will contrast momentary prosperity with lasting success.
Ittanno yeiguani focoru means exulting in momentary glory or prosperity. The Portuguese infinitive is Florecer, not OCR Floreces, and its alternative ter continues below.
Proſperidade completes ter and specifies prosperity that is very brief or small. This completes the example rather than defining another sense of ittann independently.
This separate Ittan is equated with Fitoaſa, one morning. Enlargement places the tilde over the first a in menhãa; the supplied guide's general nhaã pattern does not justify moving this copy's mark.

runs.text: Hum breuißimo eſpaço, como em quã

lines.note: Ittanji denotes an extremely brief interval. The visible u in breuißimo corrects OCR brenißimo; quã continues as quanto on the next row, retaining the abbreviation.
To completes quãto. The time needed to give a finger-flick illustrates the tiny interval; paparote is retained as the Portuguese example rather than replaced with a modern synonym.
Itten is a tiny written mark or point, glossed as a til or ponto. This is the dot/mark entry, distinct from the universal-domain compound immediately below.
Ittenca denotes the whole world or realm. The printed Todo mundo lacks an article, which is not supplied from modern Portuguese usage.
Itten xicai has the same all-encompassing meaning as the preceding Ittenca. Idem refers to that immediately preceding definition, not to the earlier point or dot.
Itteqi is equated with Fitoxizzucu, one drop. Initial capital I is visible; Miz- starts the water example and joins zu on the following physical row.
Miz- plus zu gives mizzu, water; saqe supplies the alternative liquid. The Portuguese translation begins a drop of water or wine and continues below.
Vinho completes the liquid pair. Itteqimo tabenu is a negative example, refusing even one drop, followed by an explanation of its drinking context.

runs.text: tempo do Sacazzuqui. i, Nem hũa gota de

lines.note: The refusal is said at the time of the Sacazzuqui, the drinking-cup occasion. The scan supports Sacazzuqui rather than Sacozzuqui; i introduces the Portuguese paraphrase, not another Japanese form.
Vinho bebo completes the emphatic negative: I do not drink even a drop of wine. The narrow line remains a separate continuation.
This homophonous Itteqi is a single flute, explicitly equated with Fitofuye. It must not be merged with the preceding drop-of-liquid entry.
Ittǒ is explained by Sanomi, that much or so much. The abbreviation i takes a comma here; It- begins the example's repeated headword at the physical line ending.
It- plus tǒ completes the example, glossed as do not mock so much. The scan gives a caron, not the draft's circumflex. Final upright X marks regional usage; yejecuna is retained as printed.
Ittǒ is a single company or band of people. The scan gives Fitotçuno, not Firotçuno, and the complete Portuguese companhia, including the letters near the rule.

The main text completes the company-of-people entry. The separate far-right ( ra. S. belongs to the following boat-pole definition: ra completes its final va, and S is its written-register label. Physical placement is preserved rather than silently reading the fragment into the wrong entry.

runs.text: Vara da ẽbarcação, ou o leuar Fune à va

lines.note: This Ittǒ concerns a boat-pole or propelling a boat with one. Fune is embedded in the Portuguese gloss. Final va is completed by the displaced ra. above; the headword has two t letters.
Ittô denotes comprehensive unity or inclusion: everything without leaving anything out. The full Portuguese sentence is italic; the draft's isolated roman T was a typeface-segmentation error.
Tencauo ittôni voſamuru illustrates governing the whole realm together. The Portuguese translation begins Gouer-, continued below; the example retains its circumflex in ittôni.

runs.text: nar toda a Tenca ſem ficar nada.

lines.note: Nar completes Gouernar and reiterates governing the entire Tenca without omission. Tenca is a Japanese term occurring inside the Portuguese sentence.
This separate Ittô is one light or lamp, paraphrased by Fitotçuno tomoxibi. It is distinct from the preceding comprehensive-unity entry despite matching romanized spelling.
Lanterna aceſa completes the alternatives, a candle or a lit lantern. The scan shows a single word lanterna, not the OCR's lanter na.
Ittǒ is explained by Fitoxij, equal or alike. Ittǒ xite is the example, paraphrased by Ichimi xite across the break; the scan has Ittǒ rather than the malformed OCR Iitǒ.
Mi completes Ichimi. The Portuguese explains acting uniformly or in agreement, supplying the sense of both Japanese example forms.
Ittocu is one benefit or good, paraphrased by Fitotçuno tocu. Hũ and bẽ remain abbreviated with their printed tildes.
Ittǒrai means news or a message. The example repeats Ittǒ- across the physical break; the scan supports tt, not the OCR's Iutǒ-.

Raiuo matçu completes waiting for news. The Cami-region equivalent is Iſsǒuo matçu; the damaged first s-type is read as long ſ followed by short s, not the OCR's second capital I. This graphic choice remains qualified in the uncertainty record.

runs.text: Eſperar por hũa noua, ou recado.

lines.note: Tçu completes matçu. The Portuguese translation, waiting for news or a message, supports both the preceding headword example and its regional equivalent.
Ittǒ riǒdan is cutting something into two. Item introduces a second fencing-related sense, rather than a new unrelated entry.

runs.text: Hum tempo, ou lição de eſgrima.

lines.note: The second sense is a fencing movement, timing, or lesson. The row closes the I-before-T vocabulary before the internal I-before-V heading.
Iua means rock or rocky ground; Iua ganjeqi is an equivalent continuing onto the next row. The initial I is enlarged over two rows and was lost by OCR; the following V is genuinely uppercase.
Qi completes ganjeqi, giving the equivalent rock expression. Idem refers to the preceding rock definition; the neighboring enlarged I belongs to the row above, not to this text.

runs.text: Muſgos que eſtão ſobre as rochas,

lines.note: Iuadogaxiua is described as moss-like growth on rocks or stones. The botanical description is preserved without assigning a modern taxon.

runs.text: ou penedos com algũas mellas brancas que pare

lines.note: The rock growth is further described by white marks or notches, mellas, showing on its exterior. Pare continues as parecem; the right-edge inspection shows no separate hyphen after the e.
Cem completes parecem: the white features show externally. Final upright P is the poetic-use label, not part of the italic Portuguese sentence.

runs.text: Nuuẽs que aparecem à maneira de

lines.note: Iuagumo denotes clouds resembling rocky formations. Nuuẽs retains the historical spelling and nasal abbreviation; the visual description continues below.

runs.text: rochedo hum pouco abertas, & còradas, depo

lines.note: The clouds are described as partly open and coloured after overcast weather. The grave in còradas and the break depo / is are preserved without regularizing the word division.

runs.text: is de eſtar o tempo toldado, as quaesſão ſinal do

lines.note: Is completes depois. The clouds appear after the weather has been clouded over, and are said to be a sign of the improvement described on the next row.
The sign is that the weather will settle and clear. This completes the dictionary's weather observation, not a new entry or a present-day forecast.
Iuai is the noun for a feast or celebration, matched by feſta and ſolemnidade. The following row begins its related verb separately.
Iuai, iuǒ, iuǒta gives the celebration verb. Initial I is not long ſ; Xǒ- begins the New Year example, with its caron retained.
Xǒguachino fiuo iuǒ means celebrating New Year's Day. The scan gives primeiro, not OCR primeitro; the Portuguese phrase continues with the year below.

Anno completes the New Year gloss with two n letters. The next example invites a celebratory cup of drink; qi- continues the honorific verb below. The faint trace above Iuote's o is insufficient to replace the baseline with a confidently accented form.

runs.text: Se diz no tempo do Xòguachi,

lines.note: Coximeſarei completes qicoximeſarei, the respectful invitation to drink. The Portuguese places it at Xòguachi; the local grave-mark reading in that embedded term is retained.

runs.text: ou dalgũas vodas, &c. Por feſta bebei hũa

lines.note: Weddings are another setting for the invitation. The imperative is bebei, drink, not OCR bebet; its final object continues on the following row.
Vez de vinho completes the invitation to take one drink in celebration. The terminal punctuation is retained from the locally aligned reading.

runs.text: Feſta, ou dia ſanto: palaura que corre

lines.note: Iuaibi is a feast day or holy day. The explanation introduces a qualification about church vocabulary, which continues below.

runs.text: na Igreja, por que os dias de feſta de Iapão,

lines.note: The term is said to circulate in the church; ordinary Japanese festival days are contrasted with it. Second-pass inspection confirms the capital I in Igreja. Igreja and Iapão remain Portuguese words, not Japanese font-toggle terms.
Iuaino fi supplies the contrasting Japanese expression for festival days. It is presented as a standalone cited expression after ſe dizem, not treated as an embedded noun inside a Portuguese clause.

runs.text: Eſpaço dantre a penedia, ou rochedo.

lines.note: Iuama is the interval or crevice between rocks. The Portuguese dantre construction is retained as printed.
Iuanami means waves striking a rock. The abbreviated q̃ is retained, and upright P marks poetic usage rather than belonging to the gloss.
Iuanya is an adverb expressing how much more, an a-fortiori comparison. The faint n remains supported by its visible traces and the coherent Japanese form.
Iuaqi means rocks and trees or wood. Qiyomo- starts the personal name in the example, which uses this pair figuratively for hardness of heart.

runs.text: rinjua qide naqereba ſaſuga auareni vo-

lines.note: The example says the named person is not unfeeling like wood or stone and nevertheless feels pity. The damaged opening rinjua is kept provisionally: the intended iua-qi expression is clear from the headword and gloss, but those semantic clues do not authorize silently repairing the printed sequence.
Mouaretato completes the verb divided after vo-. Feiq. cites the Heike source, followed by italic Lib. 1; the Portuguese translation begins with this man.

runs.text: não ſendo duro como pao, cu pedra mas ãtes teue

lines.note: The translation says he was not hard like wood or stone, but rather felt mercy. The anomalous printed-looking cu is retained instead of silently substituting the expected conjunction ou.
Miſericordia completes teue from the preceding row: he felt compassion. This confirms the figurative interpretation of the rocks-and-wood comparison.
Iuare denotes a reason, explanation, or cause. The headword begins with capital I, not OCR long ſ, and fits the surrounding iwa- vocabulary.

runs.text: Hũs cugumelos que nacem aos pès das

lines.note: Iuataqe is described as mushrooms growing at the feet of trees. The final noun aruores is on the next physical row and must be restored to the body, not discarded as furniture.
Aruores completes the Iuataqe gloss, trees at whose feet the mushrooms grow. This is ordinary body text on the same physical row as the separate Iuauo catchword, not a second catchword.
